title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 311: The Architecture of Ignorance: Rethinking Scientific Progress
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 311 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Architecture of Ignorance: Rethinking Scientific Progress

Paragraph 1. Most school textbooks say science moves forward in a simple straight line. Each group of scientists adds new facts to older work until humans know everything. However, philosopher Dr. Aris Thorne disagrees with this common view. In his book The Ignorance Ledger, Thorne argues that great discoveries do not just add answers. Instead, big discoveries open huge new areas of ignorance—things we realize we still do not know.

Paragraph 2. Thorne describes two different types of not knowing. First, 'passive ignorance' simply means a person has not learned basic facts yet. Second, 'active ignorance' is much smarter. It happens when brilliant research uncovers deep new mysteries. For example, discovering DNA did not finish the study of life; instead, it showed scientists that cell control was far more complicated than anyone had guessed.

Paragraph 3. Thorne also worries about how universities judge scientists today. Funding groups often count only how many papers a scientist prints or how fast a tool makes money. Because of this pressure, researchers choose safe, easy projects with sure results instead of bold, risky experiments.

Paragraph 4. In his final chapter, Thorne asks schools and funding teams to change. Rather than praising people who pretend to have every answer, universities should reward scientists who ask deep, original questions. Science does not remove all mystery from the world; it widens what we hope to explore next.

groups.title: Questions 1–4
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: What does Dr. Aris Thorne say about great scientific discoveries in Paragraph 1?
options: A. They prove school textbooks are always accurate.
B. They happen only once every hundred years.
C. They stop scientists from asking any more questions.
D. They reveal large new areas that we still do not understand.

steps: Đoạn 1: Khám phá lớn mở ra những vùng chưa biết mới mẻ (new areas of ignorance).

q2.text: Why does the passage mention the discovery of DNA in Paragraph 2?
options: A. To show that DNA research was too expensive for schools
B. To prove that major breakthroughs uncover bigger mysteries
C. To argue that biology is easier than physics
D. To explain how textbooks are printed for students

steps: Đoạn 2: Phát hiện DNA cho thấy tế bào phức tạp hơn mọi người tưởng rất nhiều.

q3.text: What problem does Thorne point out about funding groups in Paragraph 3?
options: A. They judge researchers mostly by numbers and quick profits.
B. They give all their money to dangerous experiments.
C. They forbid scientists from writing academic papers.
D. They hire university students instead of trained professors.

steps: Đoạn 3: Quỹ tài trợ chỉ đếm số bài báo và tốc độ kiếm tiền nhanh.

q4.text: What change does Thorne suggest in Paragraph 4?
options: A. Closing down university science departments
B. Paying scientists only for safe classroom lessons
C. Rewarding researchers who create smart new questions
D. Banning all textbooks in high schools

steps: Đoạn 4: Nên thưởng cho những nhà khoa học đặt ra các câu hỏi sâu sắc, mới mẻ.

q5.text: Dr. Aris Thorne won an international science prize for writing The Ignorance Ledger.

steps: Đoạn 1: Bài nhắc tên cuốn sách nhưng không hề nói ông có đoạt giải thưởng quốc tế hay không.

q6.text: Discovering DNA answered every remaining question about how cells work.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...did not finish the study of life... far more complicated than anyone had guessed."

q7.text: Counting papers encourages scientists to pick safe projects with predictable outcomes.

steps: Đoạn 3: "...researchers choose safe, easy projects with sure results..."

q8.text: Thorne believes scientists should hide their ignorance from the public.

steps: Đoạn 4: Ngược lại, ông khuyên nên coi trọng câu hỏi mới và không giả vờ biết hết.
